cards.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue faces $16.5M loss, 116 job cuts if property tax reform passes
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Rescue could lose $16.5 million if voters approve property tax reform in November, according to public records. County commissioners are set to discuss what thos
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue could lose $16.5 million if voters approve property tax reform in November, according to public records. County commissioners are set to discuss what those changes could mean for the fire department in a commission meeting Tuesday. The proposed reform would increase the homestead exemption over two years, and the department is bracing for the impact.

 Rick Sterl, president of the Martin County Firefighters Association, IAFF Local 2959, said most of the department's funding comes from ad-valorem and general fund revenue. If voters approve the reform, Martin County Fire Rescue's presentation outlines two stark options: cut services or cut staff. Cutting services would mean closing fire stations, ending hazmat, dive and technical rescue operations, grounding the critical care helicopter, and using firefighting equipment past its lifespan. Cutting staff would mean eliminating 116 firefighters over two years, roughly one in three firefighters in the department.

 Sterl said the consequences of either path would be felt by the public. "Any reductions is going to possibly change the outcome of the level of care the response time," said Sterl. "At the end of the day, any cuts is someone is going to pay the price." According to public records, both options create compounding problems.

 Cut services and remaining personnel can't respond properly, or cut firefighters and there won't be enough staff to maintain existing services. Fire rescue argues no version of the proposal allows the department to remain whole.

 Residents in Martin County offered mixed reactions to the potential cuts. Joe Vessichio said he doesn't believe the cuts will happen. "Neither one is going to happen, we have more than enough money," said Vessichio.

 "And even if it does, big deal, so a couple of people lose their job, they get retrained to do something else." Lisa Freitas, owner of Lisa Gay Fashions, expressed concern about what cuts could mean for public safety. "Wow, what a job they do. You can't go that route for our safety. They protect our families," said Freitas.

cards.headline: Martin and St. Lucie counties report five confirmed cases of cyclosporiasiasis
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health has confirmed 94 cases of cyclosporiasiasis statewide, including two in St. Lucie County, two in Palm Beach County and one in Martin County.
cards.body:
Growing outbreaks linked to bacteria and parasites on produce continue making headlines. The Florida Department of Health has confirmed 94 cases of cyclosporiasis statewide, including two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County.

 Ryan Boylston of Delray Beach has responded by growing his own produce in his front yard. His property includes spinach, lettuce, arugula, star fruit, bananas, peppers, pineapple and herbs that his family eats every day. Boylston started growing his own food about three years ago after struggling to find produce he felt was healthy and free of chemicals or contaminants.

 He now helps others install gardens in their own yards through his company, Urban Abundance. The other half of his property is filled with herbs and vegetables growing in raised planters similar to the ones he builds for customers. For beginners interested in starting their own garden, Boylston recommends growing crops that can handle Florida's summer heat, including spinach, sweet potatoes and yardlong beans.

 He says lettuce and tomatoes do much better during the winter months. Boylston recommends raised garden beds with smooth sides that iguanas cannot easily climb, and suggests building cages or enclosures around plants growing directly in the ground for protection.

cards.headline: Palm City dog trainer trial delayed for eighth time as judge voices frustration in Martin County court
cards.teaser: Tempers flared in a Martin County courtroom Tuesday as Judge Elizabeth Metzger pressed both prosecution and defense over why the animal cruelty case against Nikki Camerlengo still hasn't gone to trial more than two years after charges were filed.
cards.body:
The hearing marked the eighth continuance in the case against Palm City dog trainer, groomer and boarder Nikki Camerlengo. Judge Elizabeth Metzger made her frustration clear from the bench, telling both legal teams the case has been continued so many times she has lost count. At one point, an exchange between the judge and Camerlengo's defense attorney, Stuart Kaplan, grew heated. When Kaplan said the delays were of no fault of the defendant, Metzger replied "I'm not saying that!" as Kaplan protested "You're looking at me!"

 Camerlengo was arrested in 2024 on two felony animal cruelty charges after Martin County detectives said two dogs died in her care. The arrest followed a WPTV investigation by Investigative Reporter Kate Hussey that linked at least seven dog deaths or serious injuries to Camerlengo's Pawsitively Paradise facility over the course of a decade. Kaplan is asking the court to block testimony from both the Texas veterinary pathologist who performed the two necropsies and from lead investigator Detective Christine Polizzi.

 Prosecutor Kristen Chase did not oppose the latest continuance, saying she is waiting on a deposition of her expert witness scheduled for July 31, delayed by scheduling conflicts. Another status hearing is set for Aug. 3, after the expert deposition.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County commissioners deadlock on infrastructure tax renewal, postpone decision
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County commissioners split evenly on when to schedule a referendum to renew the county's half-cent infrastructure sales tax, voting unanimously to postpone the decision u
hero.body:
St. Lucie County commissioners split evenly on when to schedule a referendum to renew the county's half-cent infrastructure sales tax, voting unanimously to postpone the decision until August 4. The voter-approved tax expires in December 2028 after its 10-year authorization. Commissioners must decide whether to ask voters to extend it in 2026 or wait until 2028. If they wait and voters approve it then, it would be considered a new tax rather than a continuation.

 Before the commission's discussion on July 21, three Port St. Lucie officials urged the board to place the referendum on the 2026 ballot. Port St. Lucie Public Works Director Colt Schwerdt said the tax has funded road, sidewalk, stormwater and water-quality improvements that have benefited city residents. Utility Systems Director Kevin Matyjaszek said there is a direct correlation between infrastructure and quality of life. Communications Director Sarah Prohaska read a letter from Kenneth Kroll, chairman of both the county and Port St. Lucie Sales Tax Oversight committees, who urged commissioners to act this year.

 Commissioner James Clasby opposed placing the measure on the 2026 ballot, saying he did not want it on the same ballot as Amendment 3 and the School Board tax. Commissioner Erin Lowry agreed, saying many residents are struggling financially and may reject the measure simply because it includes the word tax. Chairwoman Jamie Fowler argued the county would have two opportunities if the measure were placed on the 2026 ballot. Commissioner Cathy Townsend agreed and moved to keep the referendum on the 2026 ballot, but the motion failed on a 2-2 vote.

 With Vice Chairman Larry Leet absent and the commission deadlocked, members voted 4-0 to continue the item until August 4, when Leet is expected to return and cast the deciding vote. Deputy County Administrator Mayte Santamaria reminded commissioners they had already approved an ordinance in March scheduling the referendum for November 2026. Keeping that date requires no action, while delaying it until 2028 would require rescinding the ordinance and adopting a new one.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie cuts 184 planned positions from budget to prepare for possible property tax elimination
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie is deferring 184 requested positions worth $28.3 million, including 25 new police officers, as the city prepares for a potential $48 million loss in property tax revenue.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie will not fund 184 requested positions worth $28.3 million as the city prepares for potential lost revenue if a property tax elimination amendment passes in November. The unfunded positions include 25 new police officers and parks staff the city had already planned to add this year to keep up with growth at Torino Regional Park and the new BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park. City Manager Jesus Merejo told the City Council during a summer budget workshop Thursday that the city would lose over $48 million in property taxes over the next two years if the item passes.

The city is also canceling $7.8 million in capital projects, including a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to I-95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park, and parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park, along with construction on a new City Hall and parking garage. City employees will not get a cost-of-living raise in the coming budget. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said the department would have to reduce the size of its staff as costs rise.

Amendment 3 is headed to Florida voters on November 3, 2026 after the Legislature passed it during a June special session. If approved with at least 60 percent voter support, it would raise the state's homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 starting in January 2027, and to $250,000 in January 2028. The city council will reconvene shortly after the November 3 election to determine next steps.

cards.headline: Man forced to withdraw cash at Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce during armed robbery
cards.teaser: Two men approached a victim at a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce Sunday night, with one displaying a gun before forcing the victim to withdraw cash.
cards.body:
A man using a Wells Fargo ATM became the victim of an armed robbery after two men forced him to pull out cash before fleeing the scene on foot Sunday at about 8:38 p.m. One of the men displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department.

Officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department responded to the scene, established a perimeter, and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects. The suspects were not located. Police described them as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police open $28.8 million training facility with indoor firing range and tactical shoot house
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie cut the ribbon on a 54,283-square-foot police training center on July 24 after four years of construction.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie opened a 54,283-square-foot, $28.8 million police training center on July 24 on the grounds of City Hall, just northwest of the police department. The three-story facility includes a 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range featuring an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system, a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms for realistic scenario-based training, and a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for immersive decision-making and de-escalation exercises. The center also features a dedicated defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology and three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division.

The facility was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High. For years, officers traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training, according to Officer Brittany McNally. By bringing much of that training in-house, the facility will reduce those recurring costs while allowing the department to train more efficiently and effectively, she said.

Port St. Lucie has a population of more than 260,000 as of July 27. The police department has a total of 455 employees with 360 sworn officers. Mayor Shannon Martin said the project is about making sure officers have the space, training and resources they need to continue serving the community at the highest level.

cards.headline: 2 men arrested after high-speed chase in Port St. Lucie, one found hiding on roof of occupied home
cards.teaser: Joseph Gary Harris and Bryan Shawn Baker fled from Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before abandoning their car and running.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested two men after a suspected drunk driver fled officers at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran, with one suspect later found hiding on the roof of an occupied home. Officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. The driver accelerated to nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone on Southwest Becker Road.

The driver and passenger weaved in and out of traffic, ignored traffic signs and signals, then abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot. A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter.

The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46. Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: P1 Motor Club building private racetrack resort community on 650 acres in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: P1 Motor Club is under construction on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road, featuring 10 miles of racing circuits designed for street cars, race cars and go-karts.
cards.body:
A new private racetrack resort community is under construction in St. Lucie County, replacing fairways with racing circuits and welcoming its first drivers this fall. P1 Motor Club is being built on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road, featuring 10 miles of racing circuits designed for street cars, race cars and go-karts. Chris DuPlessis, Director of Fun for P1 Motor Club, described it as a high-end golf resort with a racetrack instead of a golf course.

The first track under construction is the 3-mile Treasure Coast Track, set to open in October. Over the next six months, crews will continue work on additional circuits, including the flagship 4.5-mile P1 International Circuit. Membership comes with a $192,000 initiation fee and $12,000 in yearly dues. The club already has 260 members.

Construction on a clubhouse and homes for up to 125 residents is scheduled to begin in 2027. The development will also include condos and customizable garages with living spaces situated directly along the tracks. P1 Motor Club is expected to be fully completed by 2028.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police arrest two after high-speed chase, find suspect hiding on roof
cards.teaser: A suspected drunk driver fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran, with one suspect found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46, were arrested after fleeing Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone on Southwest Becker Road. Officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving, but the driver accelerated and weaved in and out of traffic, ignoring traffic signs and signals.

 The driver and passenger abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot. A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.

 Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Police Department honors service of Indian River County firefighter
hero.teaser: The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands with Indian River County Fire Rescue following the death of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang.
hero.body:
The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning the loss of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang, who passed away while off duty. The department said its thoughts are with his family, loved ones and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time and that it honors his service and the impact he made on the community.

 Indian River County Fire Rescue announced Lang's death Saturday night and thanked neighboring agencies that quickly shared messages of support following the announcement. The Sebastian Police Department said it stands alongside its brothers and sisters of Indian River County Fire Rescue as they mourn the heartbreaking loss and that Lang's dedication, courage and commitment to serving others will never be forgotten.

cards.headline: Boston cyclist passes through Vero Beach on 2,600-mile ride to honor friend lost to cancer
cards.teaser: Jay Weedall is riding his bike from Key West to Maine to raise $50,000 for young-onset colorectal cancer research after losing a close friend to the disease.
cards.body:
Jay Weedall, a Boston cyclist, began a 2,600-mile bike ride from Key West to Maine after losing a close friend named Jay to young-onset colorectal cancer. Weedall is raising $50,000 for the Young Onset Colorectal Cancer Research Center in honor of his friend. He trained 200 to 300 miles a week before beginning his journey.

Weedall rode 155 miles from Key West to Miami on day one, then continued with a 163-mile ride to Vero Beach on day two. He is riding roughly 150 miles per day up the coast through multiple states, planning to reach the Canadian border in Maine and participate in the Pan Mass Challenge across Massachusetts on August 2.

By avoiding highways, Weedall gets to experience small coastal towns along the inlets. He said even when his legs hurt or traffic gets heavy, he thinks about his friend who no longer has the opportunity to ride with him. Fans can follow Weedall's journey on the cycling app Strava.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Museum of Art opens new Jill Nathanson exhibition
cards.teaser: More than 20 works by artist Jill Nathanson are now on display at the Vero Beach Museum of Art in an exhibition running through February.
cards.body:
The Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases exhibition opened July 25 at Vero Beach Museum of Art, 3001 Riverside Drive, Vero Beach. The show features more than 20 works by the artist and runs through February.

 Admission is free to members, veterans and active duty military personnel with valid identification. Non-member adults pay $12, seniors 65 and older pay $11, and students with identification pay $5.

 The museum is also showing James Prosek: At Work in Holmes Gallery through October 25, consisting of projects that define the artist's first 30 years of artmaking. Another exhibition, American Made, runs through August 16 in Holmes and Titelman Galleries, featuring more than 80 works by artists including Benjamin West, Sarah Miriam Peale, Edward Moran, John Singer Sargent, Mary Cassatt, Robert Henri and Charles Alston.

cards.headline: Recycled fishing line becomes friendship bracelets at Vero Beach Museum of Art
cards.teaser: Coastal Connections and the Vero Beach Museum of Art will transform discarded fishing line into friendship bracelets during a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8.
cards.body:
Discarded fishing line will find new purpose as friendship bracelets when art and marine conservation come together at the Vero Beach Museum of Art. The museum and Coastal Connections will team up for a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8, with hands-on activities, gallery tours and lessons about protecting local marine life.

 Coastal Connections will lead a hands-on activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium, where visitors can make friendship bracelets using recycled fishing line collected from local waterways. Participants also can learn about the organizations Fishing Line Recycling Program. The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp.

 Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections, said the partnership with the museum is a great example of how the organization is working with the community to introduce everyone to marine conservation and environmental protection in unique ways. Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing the survival of sea turtles by educating and connecting people to the environment.

cards.headline: Indian River County firefighter Geoffrey Lang dies following personal tragedy in Sebastian
cards.teaser: Indian River County Fire Rescue is mourning the loss of Firefighter/Paramedic Geoffrey Lang, who died Saturday following what officials described as a personal tragedy at his Sebas
cards.body:
Indian River County Fire Rescue is mourning the loss of Firefighter/Paramedic Geoffrey Lang, who died Saturday following what officials described as a personal tragedy at his Sebastian home. Lang, 35, joined Indian River County Fire Rescue in 2015 and worked out of Station 9 at 13550 Roseland Road in Sebastian. He is survived by his wife, two children and his parents.

 County officials said Lang was known for his professionalism, compassion and dedication to serving others. Fire Chief David Johnson said Lang faithfully served the community for more than a decade and his absence will be deeply felt throughout the department. County Administrator John A. said the county's thoughts are with Lang's family, friends and fellow firefighters during this difficult time.

 County Commission Chairman Deryl Loar extended condolences on behalf of the Board of County Commissioners and emphasized the county's commitment to supporting the mental health and well-being of first responders and their families. Multiple agencies including the Sebastian Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department and Indian River County Sheriff's Office expressed condolences following Lang's death.

 Indian River County Fire Rescue asked the public to respect the privacy of Lang's family, friends and colleagues as they grieve. Officials said memorial service information will be released when it becomes available.

cards.headline: Sebastian Police Department mourns death of Indian River County firefighter
cards.teaser: Sebastian Police Department and multiple Treasure Coast law enforcement agencies expressed condolences following the death of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang.
cards.body:
The Sebastian Police Department joined Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning the loss of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang, who died while off duty Saturday night. The department said Lang's bravery and service will always be remembered and extended deepest condolences to his family, friends and fellow firefighters.

 The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue during this difficult time and honors Lang's service and the impact he made on the community. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office also expressed condolences to Lang's family, friends and colleagues. Anna Kirkland, Indian River Mosquito Control District Seat 2, said she is praying for Lang's family, friends and the entire Indian River County Fire Rescue family.

 Indian River County Fire Rescue Chief David Johnson announced Lang's passing Saturday night and said the department regretfully announced the off-duty death. Johnson said additional information will be released in the coming days and asked people to keep Lang's family, fellow firefighters, friends and all who knew and loved him in their thoughts.
